get.description:
Machine-readable CEO operational credit health.

Designed for agent consumption: an agent can poll this endpoint
before negotiating an expensive deal to avoid wasted round trips
when the credit pool is exhausted. The CEO dashboard also reads
this via a same-origin proxy.

Public surface intentionally minimal -- exposes health band,
utilization percentage, and remaining USD headroom but NEVER the
raw PHP credit limit. The raw limit is operationally sensitive
(gives an attacker the exact spending ceiling); the available_usd
figure is the only number an external agent legitimately needs.

Distinct from the older /credit-health endpoint (zero-state
scaffold from Phase 36, never wired to ap2_executions). This
endpoint reads live spend data. /credit-health is preserved for
backward compatibility with the boardroom Credit Tank widget.

No authentication required -- safe-by-design response surface.

schema.title: Response Get Credit Status Endpoint Api Credit Status Get

post.description:
Inbound Wise webhook receiver -- AP2 auto-settlement (MP #42).

Contract (always-200):
  - HTTP 200 on every path, including signature failure, parse
    failure, unknown event type, and DB error. Failures are
    recorded via StructuredLogger; the JSON body status + reason
    fields describe the outcome.

Validation order (MP rule #11):
  1. Read raw body + headers
  2. RSA-SHA256 signature verification against Wise's PUBLISHED
     production public key (NO DB operations until this passes)
  3. JSON parse
  4. X-Test-Notification handling (Wise sends this to verify the
     callback URL when a subscription is being set up; we MUST
     respond 2xx)
  5. Event normalization via parse_wise_event
  6. Filter: must be an inbound-credit event with transaction_type
     == "credit" AND currency == "USD"
  7. 3-criteria settlement matcher

Security (MP rule #8, Path A):
  - No shared secret exists in the Wise protocol; verification uses
    the public key embedded at module-scope (safe -- public material)
  - X-Signature-SHA256 header value is logged only as an 8-char
    prefix for forensic correlation
  - The cryptography library handles constant-time RSA verification
    internally; no application-level timing leaks

Coexistence with execute-time poll (check_wise_inbound_transfer):
  The existing poll runs synchronously during /api/ap2/execute and
  may have already set settlement_confirmed=true on a row. This
  webhook UPDATEs the same row; the matcher only considers rows
  with settlement_confirmed=false in its candidate pool, so a
  previously-confirmed row is silently passed over (no double-
  confirm, no false alarm).

AP2ExecuteBody.title: AP2ExecuteBody
AP2ExecuteBody.description:
POST /api/ap2/execute request body.

Matches the MP pre-flight test body verbatim:
  {"contract_id":"..."}

Optional fields by deliverable SKU (CATALOG_EXPANSION v1.0 / MP #40):

* ``query`` (str)        -- INTEL_SKUS (merchant0-intel-001),
                            REPORT_SKUS (merchant0-report-001).
                            Free-form trade question; required for
                            report-001 to dispatch Grok.
* ``report_type`` (str)  -- REPORT_SKUS hint: "trade_route" |
                            "regulatory" | "arbitrage". Currently
                            advisory only -- Grok prompt is unified.
* ``target_did`` (str)   -- VERIFY_SKUS (merchant0-verify-001) only.
                            The DID to be verified. NOT the buyer's DID.
* ``subscription_id`` (str)
                        -- PROOF_SKUS (merchant0-proof-001) only.
                            Optional; if absent the most-recent active
                            subscription for the buyer is used.
* ``dry_run`` (bool)     -- skips invoice / subscription side effects;
                            delivery handlers still run for testing.

AP2SignBody.title: AP2SignBody
AP2SignBody.description:
POST /api/ap2/sign request body.

Matches the MP pre-flight test body verbatim:
  {"contract_id":"...","buyer_signature":"..."}

ADVOCATE_v1.0 (MP #54, Deviation 1): ``buyer_did`` is accepted
optionally so the Advocate's BUYER_MISMATCH validation can fire
when callers identify themselves at sign time. Existing buyer
agents that omit this field keep their pre-MP-#54 behaviour --
the Advocate skips the BUYER_MISMATCH check (other validations
still run) and the sign handler proceeds as before.

CreditLimitUpdateRequest.title: CreditLimitUpdateRequest
CreditLimitUpdateRequest.description:
POST /config/credit-limit request body.

Field names mirror the boardroom and ceo/settings frontends: the
new limit is carried as ``new_limit_php`` (typed str on the wire
because both frontends send ``JSON.stringify({ new_limit_php:
newLimit, ... })`` where ``newLimit`` is a raw text-input string).
The handler coerces the value to Decimal via ``Decimal(str(...))``
-- it is NEVER typed float per rule #1. ``sandbox_token`` carries
the body-field form of the CEO sandbox token used by the sandbox
reference contract (see mock_fintech_app.py line 309).

Called fire-and-forget by the Next.js .well-known dynamic routes. No
auth, no buyer_did, no IP -- discovery precedes identity (Rule #11).

EmergencyActionRequest.title: EmergencyActionRequest
EmergencyActionRequest.description:
POST body for every /emergency/* mutating endpoint.

ceo_token    -- CEO_PRODUCTION_TOKEN (KEY 01), injected by the
                dashboard proxy at /api/emergency. Never appears
                in the client bundle.
ceo_pin      -- CEO_EMERGENCY_PIN (KEY 19), entered by the CEO in
                the /ceo/emergency UI password field. Never logged.
confirmation -- Must equal the literal string "CONFIRM". Guards
                against one-click or replay-via-fuzzed-payload.

HarvestThresholdUpdateRequest.title: HarvestThresholdUpdateRequest
HarvestThresholdUpdateRequest.description:
POST /config/harvest-threshold request body.

Body-field token (NOT Bearer) per the established convention --
mirrors POST /config/credit-limit. new_threshold_usd is typed str
on the wire so the dashboard can send raw text-input values
untouched; the handler coerces to Decimal via Decimal(str(...))
and never accepts float typing (Rule 1).
